Marathon #5 on the year done.

Twin Cities Marathon was a fantastic marathon. I learn a little bit more after each race, and can appreciate what lengths well-run events go to in order to make the run as good as possible.

The great:

  • Nearly the entire race was supported by fans. I've never seen anything like it. I didn't run fast as I was with my cousin in her first run, so we were catching the tail end of the enthusiasm in some stretches. Despite that, they were still cheering and encouraging all the runners. It was awesome. They also had the bells ringing at a huge church near the start of the race. I think I was more impressed than anyone else, but it really stood out.

  • The course itself was beautiful. Rounding several lakes, beautiful neighborhoods, gorgeous architecture....it really was beautiful. Better than either Portland or Dallas, both of which would be comparable, but neither quite as good.

The Okay:

  • In the transitions between lakes, the lanes get pretty narrow. If you're shooting for a PR, and don't start near the front, you may struggle there.

  • Support was a little less than what I would've expected. They had drink stations every 1.5ish miles. In the limited training I had for this run, I trained to drink every 1.5 miles, but even with that I felt a bit more taxed at then end than I expected to. More frequent drink stations in certain stretches could've helped.

Overall:

  • It was a great marathon, and I'm glad I went. Anyone in the area interested in running a full should definitely consider this one, especially as a first race. Again, the support even for those near the back was phenomenal.
